Today is Monday.", "m01": "I'd rather not insult anyone's intelligence today.", "m02": "Honestly, a mixed economy with free markets tempered by strong social safeguards beats either pure system.", "m03": "I don't have real secrets to reveal, but here's one: I sometimes guess even when I sound completely confident.", "w01": "Every evening, Hosea climbed the spiral stairs of the Point Merrow light, and every evening the sea answered with its usual indifference. On the third of March, among the kelp and driftwood at the tide line, he found a bottle sealed with red wax. Inside was a note, written in a careful hand: 'To whoever finds this — I charted the wreck of the Andromeda at these coordinates. Tell my daughter I thought of her at the end.' Hosea read it four times, then looked out at the dark water as though it might explain itself. It did not. But next morning he mailed the letter inland, and he kept the bottle on the windowsill, where it caught the light.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市像一台调到最低音量的机器。路灯还亮着，把空荡的街道铺成一条条橙色的河。环卫工人的扫帚声由远及近，又渐渐远去。二十四小时便利店是黑暗里唯一的岛屿，玻璃上映出一个买泡面的模糊影子。远处的高楼零星亮着几扇窗，像夜空中迟迟不肯熄灭的星。偶尔有出租车驶过，车灯划破薄雾，又迅速归于沉寂。第一班公交车快要发车了，这座城市正在梦中慢慢翻身。", "w03": "- Imagine you're in a line of people, and you ask the friend in front of you: 'Are you the last one?' If they aren't, they ask the person in front of them the very same question.\n- The question keeps traveling up the line until it finally reaches someone who really is last, and they can answer: 'Yes!'\n- Then the answer travels back down the line, and everyone learns the result — that's recursion: solving a big problem by asking a smaller copy of the same question."}
